title: RDP logon (type 10) to SCRANTON by pbeesly from 172.18.39.2
rationale: Logon type 10 with User32/Negotiate on SCRANTON is an RDP session; source attribution is uncertain, hence suspicious.

title: PsExec SMB/ADMIN$ lateral movement from SCRANTON to NASHUA with cleartext credentials
rationale: Both findings describe the same PsExec64.exe executions from SCRANTON against \\NASHUA passing explicit pbeesly credentials, producing PSEXESVC service installs and 4648 explicit-credential logons over SMB/ADMIN$. Best fit is SMB/Windows Admin Shares remote service execution.

title: pbeesly network logons to NEWYORK and IPC$/samr access from SCRANTON and NASHUA
rationale: Remote SMB/RPC authentication and IPC$/samr access to NEWYORK by the compromised account fits SMB/Windows Admin Shares; no execution observed, hence suspicious.

title: PowerShell remoting (WinRM/5985) from SCRANTON to NASHUA
rationale: Invoke-Command -ComputerName NASHUA over TCP 5985 from SCRANTON to NASHUA is Windows Remote Management lateral movement.

title: python.exe written to \\NASHUA\ADMIN$ and executed remotely via PsExec
rationale: pbeesly wrote Temp\python.exe into NASHUA's ADMIN$ share (WriteData) which was then executed on the target, matching taint of shared content.

title: PSEXESVC remote service execution on NASHUA launching unsigned python.exe
rationale: Both findings describe the same repeated PSEXESVC service installs on NASHUA spawning C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe as pbeesly; remote service execution via PsExec fits exploitation of remote services.

title: PsExec used from SCRANTON to copy PSEXESVC.exe and python.exe to NASHUA over ADMIN$
rationale: Tool transfer of PSEXESVC.exe and python.exe to NASHUA over ADMIN$ is lateral tool transfer.

title: Hands-on lateral movement scranton->nashua via PsExec; no software deployment tool used
rationale: Finding documents PsExec-based lateral movement and explicitly notes no SCCM/Intune/WSUS activity, so T1072 does not fit; the observed action is SMB/ADMIN$ remote service execution.

title: Compromised pbeesly session on SCRANTON used WinRM/PsExec to move to NASHUA and NEWYORK
rationale: Finding covers the initial compromise chain plus subsequent lateral movement; the lateral action described is WinRM/PsExec, best represented as Windows Remote Management.

title: Encoded PowerShell payload (IEX from bitmap pixels) on SCRANTON
rationale: Steganographic/encoded PowerShell loader executed as pbeesly is execution, not lateral movement; best ATT&CK fit is PowerShell.
